review.tagline: MLOps course with code for training, tuning, and serving a text classifier
review.summary: A course repository that walks through building a text classifier end to end: a Jupyter notebook, then refactored Python scripts for training, tuning, evaluation, inference and serving. It uses Ray for distributed workloads, MLflow for experiment tracking, pytest for code, data and model tests, and Anyscale Jobs and Services for production deployment.
review.audience: Developers and data scientists learning to take ML from notebook to production
strengths: Covers the full path: notebook, scripts, tests, MLflow tracking, Ray Serve, CI/CD
Runs on a laptop without a GPU, with configurable worker counts
Separate pytest suites for code, data and trained models
Plain Python scripts with documented CLI arguments for each workload
weaknesses: Production section depends on Anyscale (account, CLI token, S3 upload paths)
Example task is a small text classifier, not an LLM application
Setup is built around Ray; other stacks need adaptation
README promotes a paid live cohort
needs: Needs Ray, MLflow, Anyscale, AWS S3, pytest, pre-commit
